title: Pulseaudio Volume Control (pa-applet) wakes up all audio devices when opening
line: Opening the Audio Volume popup no longer wakes up suspended audio devices to show their level meters.
explanation: Each slider's level meter opens a record stream on the device's monitor, and that stream kept a suspended device awake. Harald's fix (PA_STREAM_DONT_INHIBIT_AUTO_SUSPEND) was reverted over a memory leak: on PipeWire such a stream stays in CREATING until the device wakes up, and the existing teardown only disconnects a CREATING stream on its next state change, so every popup close left one stream behind in pipewire (about 3.5 MB each, 12 after 30 opens on the rig). The change re-adds the flag and parks a stream dropped while still connecting, so the next meter of the same device reuses it instead of opening another; parked streams are released as soon as they connect or fail.

commits.message:
volumemonitor: don't wake up devices, reuse streams still connecting

The meter streams kept suspended devices awake. Not inhibiting suspend
leaked them, as they only connect once their device wakes, so keep the
dropped ones and let the next meter of that device reuse them instead.

BUG: 507212

media.caption: Master: popup open, nothing playing. The null sink b27c wakes from SUSPENDED to IDLE because of the meter stream.
Fix: same popup, the meter stream is attached but b27c stays SUSPENDED.
Master: slider idle (top) and while a tone plays (bottom), the darker meter segment shows the level.
Fix: the meter still shows the level when audio starts while the popup is open (top idle, bottom playing).

review.text: Re-adding PA_STREAM_DONT_INHIBIT_AUTO_SUSPEND while addressing PipeWire's stuck PA_STREAM_CREATING teardown leak is the right problem to solve in plasma-pa, and the screenshots confirm the sink stays suspended while peak metering still works. However, the parked-stream implementation has two real C++/libpulse hazards: the state callback calls pa_stream_disconnect(s) before clearing the state callback—causing a re-entrant callback that erases and unrefs s before the outer call touches s again—and s_connectingStreams is an unmanaged file-scope static QHash with static destruction order UB and leaked stream refs on shutdown. Additionally, the author noted an unexplained stray stream surviving a wake once, and before-2.png/after-2.png only show a single playing slider rather than the idle/playing pair described in their captions.
changes: Clear the state callback with pa_stream_set_state_callback(s, nullptr, nullptr) before calling pa_stream_disconnect(s) (and only call pa_stream_disconnect when PA_STREAM_IS_GOOD(pa_stream_get_state(s))) to prevent re-entrant invocation and use-after-unref.

Replace the unmanaged file-scope static QHash with a lifetime-managed container cleaned up on PulseAudioQt::Context teardown / QCoreApplication::aboutToQuit (clearing callbacks and unreffing any remaining parked streams).

Investigate and eliminate the wake-up race noted in testing (or consider skipping meter stream creation while a Device is SuspendedState and creating it on Device::stateChanged, which also avoids leaving parked ~3.5 MB streams in PipeWire after closing the popup).
Update before-2.png/after-2.png or their captions so the evidence accurately matches what is shown.

reviews.text: Re-adding PA_STREAM_DONT_INHIBIT_AUTO_SUSPEND is the established fix (pavucontrol does the same, and the reporter confirmed it). The patch also explains and fixes the leak behind Harald's revert: on pipewire-pulse a passive stream stays CREATING until the device wakes, and libpulse can't cancel it. Parking one CREATING stream per (source, monitored stream) key and reusing it is careful about refcounts: one ref moves into the hash, the callback erases it before unref, context failure releases it, and callbacks are cleared and re-set on reuse. The 60-cycle RSS/stream-count measurement and the meter-still-works checks back this up. Nits: if two meters ever park the same key at once, the second still leaks the old way (a QMultiHash would close that). after-2.png is a single 80 px row, not the 'top idle / bottom playing' pair its caption describes. Filing the CREATING-reply behaviour with PipeWire would be good, but it doesn't block this.
